replies.author: Maleficent_Caramel98
replies.body: The bridge and the "self healing" itself was kind of difficult. But the brain and core has everything connected and woven together thats hard to vibe code because llms love to lie. So I also made an ai accountability feature where it hydra itself keeps track of failures the llms/ai makes and knows how to fix it then feels it back to the agent

replies.author: AzimuthSystems
replies.body: that's actually the part i'm most curious about. when hydra records an ai failure, how do you stop a bad “fix” from becoming part of the memory too? do you have some kind of verification step before it feeds it back to the agent?

replies.author: Maleficent_Caramel98
replies.body: This is the fun part. I have that gauntlet I built that carries an exact replica of my pc that hosts hydra, I coded it so it morphs to anyone's computer or phone scematics.. Pretty simply it gets run through a twin sandbox universe first untill its corrected the mistake even before attempting it on anything real. Mistakes get through sometimes because llms forget things and make shit up. But I stabilize and freeze everything quite often and no real damage has ever been done..

replies.author: Maleficent_Caramel98
replies.body: What is it your working on?

replies.author: AzimuthSystems
replies.body: i'm building AZIMUTH, still pretty early. it's basically an automated market research system for crypto — collecting microstructure data, detecting setups, then testing them in paper/forward conditions. right now i'm mostly working on causal testing, data quality and making sure the system doesn't fool itself with bad labels or model output. your double-sandbox idea is interesting though, especially if the llm can break things upstream.
